papers.title: Dataset on Fatigue Results and Fatigue Fracture Initiation Site Characterization in Stress-Relieved PBF-LB/M Ti-6Al-4V Four-Point Bend and Axial Specimens: Part I (High Power, Variable Scan Velocities)
papers.abstract: As part of a NASA University Leadership Initiative (ULI) program, this work supports the continued development and evaluation of a fatigue-based process window for stress-relieved Ti-6Al-4V specimens produced via laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M). Four-point bend and axial fatigue specimens were fabricated by NASA ULI collaborators across a range of scan velocities (800–2000 mm/s) at a constant power of 370 W using an EOS M290 system. All fatigue specimens were low-stress-ground by a commercial vendor and tested at Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) under load-controlled cyclic loading at a stress ratio of R = 0.1. This paper presents a curated dataset linking PBF-LB/M process parameters to fatigue outcomes across 175 specimens. Of these, 136 fractured and this study includes fatigue crack initiation site identification and defect morphology metrics derived from post mortem SEM analysis. Specimens that reached runout (107 cycles) and did not fracture under subsequent fatigue testing are retained in the dataset, with fractographic fields marked as ‘NA’ to indicate non-applicability. The dataset includes specimen metadata, processing parameters, fatigue life data, fatigue initiation site classification (e.g., keyhole, gas-entrapped pore (GeP), lack-of-fusion (LoF), contamination), defect size and shape descriptors, and spatial location relative to the free surface. These data are intended to support defect-based fatigue life prediction, probabilistic modeling, process–structure–property studies, and machine learning frameworks linking process parameters to fatigue performance in PBF-LB/M Ti-6Al-4V.

summary_en.motivation: To support the development of a fatigue-based process window for stress-relieved Ti-6Al-4V produced by laser powder bed fusion.
summary_en.method: Four-point bend and axial fatigue specimens were fabricated at various scan velocities, tested under load-controlled cyclic loading, and post-mortem SEM analysis identified crack initiation sites and defect morphology.
summary_en.result: A curated dataset of 175 specimens links process parameters to fatigue life and fracture initiation characteristics, including defect type, size, and location.
summary_en.validation: Experimental fatigue testing (R=0.1) and fractographic characterization of 136 fractured specimens.

papers.title: Investigation of the Effect of Different Cutting Conditions on Machining Performance in Parting Off Operation Applied to Ti6Al4V Alloy on CNC Lathe
papers.abstract: Although every product produced on a lathe is subjected to parting off operation at least once, there has been almost no study on this operation. In this study, Ti6Al4V alloy, which is difficult to machine, was chosen as the work piece material to investigate the parting off operation in a confined space. The effects of different cooling conditions (dry cutting and conventional cooling), different cutting speeds (30 and 50 m/min) and different feeds (0.01, 0.02, 0.03 and 0.04 mm/rev) on surface roughness (Ra), tool wear (Vb) and chip morphology were investigated. In the experiments, it was observed that coolant application is much more vital than in open machining operations, especially in terms of tool wear, with improvements of up to 90%. The increase in cutting speed had a negative effect on Ra, but not a positive one, in contrast to open-machining operations. The increase in feeds increased Ra and Vb values, similar to the open-machining operations. In addition, the increase in feeds resulted in a shorter and more controllable chip form. These results show that machinability studies should not be limited to open-machining operations such as turning and facing, which are easy to implement. It is thought that solving the many problems encountered due to the nature of the process in confined space operations with very different and challenging conditions will add a new dimension to the studies on machinability.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本研究涉及Ti6Al4V合金的切断加工参数对表面粗糙度和刀具磨损的影响，虽未直接测量疲劳性能，但加工表面质量是影响疲劳寿命的关键因素，可为后处理工艺优化提供参考。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not measure fatigue or mechanical performance (e.g., tensile, fatigue life) after the cutting operation; it focuses on surface roughness and tool wear only.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究Ti6Al4V合金切断加工中不同切削条件对加工性能的影响。
summary_zh.method: 通过实验改变冷却条件、切削速度和进给量，测量表面粗糙度、刀具磨损和切屑形态。
summary_zh.result: 冷却液使刀具磨损改善高达90%，进给量增加产生更短更可控的切屑。
summary_zh.validation: 实际切削实验测量表面粗糙度和刀具磨损验证趋势。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of cutting parameters on machining performance during parting off of Ti6Al4V alloy.
summary_en.method: Experimental study varying cooling condition, cutting speed, and feed rate, measuring surface roughness, tool wear, and chip morphology.
summary_en.result: Coolant application improved tool wear by up to 90%, and increased feed resulted in shorter, more controllable chips.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements of surface roughness and tool wear under different conditions.
